## Objective
- Build a complete, playable open-city 3D-style browser game inspired by GTA-style urban free roam.

## Requirements
- Deliver GTA 5-scale style systems with GTA 6-inspired realistic presentation.
- Include a city, airport, trains, metro, monorail, traffic, pedestrians, helicopters, planes, vehicle entry/exit, and a phone map interface.
- Provide car damage, train control, smooth braking, aircraft/vehicle interaction, and a polished HUD.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a lightweight canvas-based pseudo-3D game rather than Unity, due to browser build constraints.
- Used a fictional “Neon Coast”/“San Paloma” setting to avoid copying GTA assets or branding.
- Added a cinematic start screen, minimap, mission panel, wanted indicator, phone UI, and desktop controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with the full game shell and HUD.
- Created `style.css` with the visual system, responsive layouts, overlays, phone UI, and controls.

- Added the start overlay, phone map, vehicle interaction, and mission dismissal.
- Added a local server on port 3002.
- Captured a viewport screenshot at `screenshots/neon-coast.jpg`.
- Verified JavaScript syntax with `node --check game.js`.
- Verified the page returns HTTP 200.

### Active
- Visual/runtime verification is active but only the initial screenshot has been reviewed.

### Blocked
- No remaining implementation blocker identified.

1. Start the game from the local server and test WASD, train boarding, vehicle entry/exit, the phone map, and responsive layouts.
2. Inspect `screenshots/neon-coast.jpg` for full-screen composition issues.
3. Fix any runtime console errors and add requested interaction details where missing.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main page structure and UI markup.
- `style.css`: Full visual styling and responsive behavior.
- `game.js`: Complete game logic and canvas rendering.
- `screenshots/neon-coast.jpg`: Initial captured viewport screenshot.
- `start.sh`: Existing project start entry point.

## Important Context
- The browser is currently running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- The game is uncommitted unless files were modified outside the captured build state.
- Controls are WASD/arrows for movement, E for enter/exit, Space for handbrake, and M for the phone.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable open-city 3D-style browser game inspired by GTA-style urban free roam, with a polished interface and broad city systems.

## Requirements
- Include a city, airport, trains, metro, monorail, traffic, pedestrians, helicopters, planes, vehicle entry/exit, and a phone map interface.
- Support car damage, train control, smooth braking, aircraft/vehicle interaction, and a polished HUD.
- Use an original fictional setting and assets rather than copying GTA branding or content.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a lightweight canvas-based pseudo-3D browser game.
- Set in the fictional “Neon Coast” / “San Paloma” city.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the game shell, styling, canvas city rendering, transport/traffic systems, movement, HUD, start overlay, phone UI, and interaction hints in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Fixed keyboard input’s `e.key.toLower` typo.
- Fixed train boarding/control to use the actual train object, follow its track, pause its autonomous movement while controlled, and use proximity checks against each train’s actual location.
- `node --check game.js` passes; `http://localhost:3002` returns HTTP 200.
- Opened the game in Playwright and confirmed the page loads and the start overlay can be dismissed.

### Active
- Finish browser-based interaction testing. Recent keyboard checks were inconclusive: pressing E did not change `#vehicleName` from `ON FOOT`; the interaction hint was not shown as active in the inspected state.

### Blocked
- No known implementation blockers.

## Next Move
1. Reload and enter the city, then test movement, phone toggle, vehicle entry/exit, and train boarding/control in the browser.
2. Investigate why E did not enter the coupe during the last browser test; verify keyboard events and distance/proximity state.
3. Review the rendered scene and responsive layouts, and fix any gameplay or visual issues found.
4. Check for runtime console errors; the only observed console error so far is a missing `/favicon.ico` (404).

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game rendering, input, interactions, and simulation logic.
- `index.html`: Game UI and page structure.
- `style.css`: Visual styling and responsive layouts.
- `screenshots/neon-coast.jpg`: Initial viewport capture.

## Important Context
- The game is served at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Controls: WASD/arrows move or drive, E enters/exits, Space handbrake, M phone.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable open-city 3D browser game set in fictional San Paloma.
- The user clarified that it must be genuinely 3D and designed for phone play, not a 2D game designed for desktop.

## Requirements
- Include a city, airport, trains, metro, monorail, traffic, pedestrians, aircraft, vehicle entry/exit, and a phone map interface.
- Support vehicle/train control and polished mobile-friendly gameplay and UI.
- Use original fictional setting and assets; do not copy GTA branding or content.

## Decisions
- The existing canvas-based pseudo-3D implementation does not meet the user’s 3D requirement; replace or substantially rebuild it as actual 3D.
- Three.js via jsDelivr was checked and returned HTTP 200.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing prototype supports city systems and interaction basics in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- Moved the coupe closer to the player in `game.js` so the interaction prompt appears on start.
- Browser smoke test passed vehicle entry/exit, driving input, phone toggle, and commuter train boarding; no browser errors observed.
- `node --check game.js` passes.

### Active
- Rework the game as actual 3D and optimize the experience for phone controls and mobile layouts.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current game files and replace the pseudo-3D canvas rendering with a true 3D scene, likely using Three.js.
2. Add touch-first mobile controls, including movement/steering and interaction buttons, and ensure the UI fits phone screens.
3. Preserve the open-city transport, traffic, pedestrian, aircraft, vehicle, and phone-map gameplay systems in the 3D implementation.
4. Test on a mobile-sized viewport and verify touch controls, rendering, and runtime errors.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Existing pseudo-3D rendering, game state, movement, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Current HUD, overlays, phone UI, and control hints.
- `style.css`: Existing layout and responsive styles.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The game was served at `http://localhost:3002`.
- The user’s latest feedback supersedes the earlier pseudo-3D implementation direction: “the game is 3D, not 2D, and the game will be played on the phone, not on the computer.”

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable open-city 3D browser game set in fictional San Paloma, designed for phone play.
- Replace the pseudo-3D canvas rendering with a genuine 3D game while retaining the city and transport gameplay.

## Requirements
- Include a city, airport, trains, metro, monorail, traffic, pedestrians, aircraft, vehicle entry/exit, and a phone map interface.
- Support vehicle/train control and polished mobile-friendly gameplay and UI.
- Use original fictional setting and assets; do not copy GTA branding or content.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js for actual 3D rendering, loaded from jsDelivr.
- Add touch-first controls alongside existing keyboard controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced the canvas-based renderer and game world in `game.js` with a Three.js scene containing roads, buildings, vehicles, pedestrians, trains, airport, and aircraft.
- Changed `index.html` to load `game.js` as a module and added touch-control markup.
- Added touch joystick, accelerate, interact, and phone-map behavior in `game.js`.
- Ran `node --check game.js`; no syntax errors were reported.

### Active
- Add responsive styling for the new touch controls and verify the game’s mobile layout.
- Test rendering, gameplay interactions, touch controls, and runtime errors in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add mobile-first CSS for `.touch-controls`, `.stick-zone`, and `.touch-button`; hide desktop keyboard hints on phone layouts.
2. Run the game in a browser at desktop and mobile viewport sizes; check WebGL rendering, interactions, and console errors.
3. Fix issues found in testing and confirm movement, driving, vehicle/train boarding, and phone-map controls.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, world systems, movement, controls, and rendering.
- `index.html`: HUD, phone UI, module script, and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Existing UI styles; touch-control styles still need implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Three.js module URL is `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.169.0/build/three.module.js`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable open-city 3D browser game set in fictional San Paloma, designed for phone play.
- Validate rendered gameplay and interactions, and fix runtime or visual issues.

## Requirements
- Include a city, airport, trains, metro, monorail, traffic, pedestrians, aircraft, vehicle entry/exit, and phone-map interface.
- Support vehicle/train control and polished mobile-friendly gameplay and UI.
- Use original fictional setting and assets; do not copy GTA branding or content.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js via jsDelivr.
- Provide touch controls alongside keyboard controls.

- `game.js`: Three.js scene, world systems, movement, controls, and rendering.

- `style.css`: UI and responsive control styling.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable open-city 3D browser game set in fictional San Paloma, designed for phone play.
- Validate gameplay and interactions, and fix any runtime or visual issues.

## Requirements
- Include a city, airport, trains, metro, monorail, traffic, pedestrians, aircraft, vehicle entry/exit, and phone-map interface.
- Support vehicle/train control and polished mobile-friendly gameplay and UI.
- Use an original fictional setting and assets; do not copy GTA branding or content.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js via jsDelivr.
- Provide touch controls alongside keyboard controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the Three.js city scene, transit, traffic, pedestrians, aircraft, HUD, phone interface, and mobile controls.
- Fixed vehicle heading/movement and mobile touch-control styling.
- Fixed `Uncaught ReferenceError: elev is not defined` in `buildStations()` by using `elevated`.
- Verified `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.
- Captured and inspected desktop/mobile screenshots; no specific visual fixes were identified.
- Started the game in Playwright and confirmed the start button works and driving updates the speed display.

### Active
- Validate interaction flow, especially entering/exiting cars, train boarding/control, phone-map behavior, and mobile touch controls.
- Investigate why pressing `e` during the recent test left the player `ON FOOT`; test start and phone states were altered through separate browser actions, so the result is inconclusive.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload the page and run a clean Playwright session through start, vehicle entry, driving, exit, phone map, and train boarding/control.
2. Test touch controls at a mobile viewport and fix any issues found.
3. Re-run syntax/diff checks and review the final changes.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, world systems, movement, controls, and rendering.
- `index.html`: HUD, phone UI, touch controls, and module script.
- `style.css`: UI and responsive control styling.
- `/tmp/opencode/neon-coast-fixed.png`: Desktop screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/neon-coast-mobile.png`: Mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in the current Git status.
- Three.js module URL: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.169.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Browser automation is available via `playwright-cli`; test server is running on port `3002`.
- The last Playwright interaction test reported `vehicle after entering: ON FOOT`, `speed: 09`, `vehicle after exit: ON FOOT`, and phone class `phone`; phone state had been manipulated during the test, so this is not yet a reliable gameplay diagnosis.

- Use Three.js via jsDelivr.
- Use shared nearest-target interaction logic, with a train at a platform prioritized over nearby road traffic.
